riddle: First, put your ear to the bucket. The closed mouths still sing.
Next, bring what was promised to the line where nothing quite dries.
Let the little numbers on the wet flank settle their account.
Give the house its due; it has kept the last card warm for you.
Now count the teeth that never belonged in any mouth below the water.
Step softly between the rusted warnings. The quiet patch is yours.
Take the gaze you can see straight through, though it sees you all the same.
The paper on the square knows which small iron tongue will turn.
Let the patient black stitches tell you what the belly will not.
Balance what we brought ashore against what the water says it weighed.
Under the striped canvas, ask what has already happened tomorrow.
Last, lay the sodden scraps together. A debt is whole again.
